scientific_intent.scientific_task: Compute complete Needleman–Wunsch global alignment score matrices using BLOSUM62 and linear gap penalties
scientific_intent.discretization: Three equal-length pairs of lengths64,96,32, gap penalties10,3,2. Native libc seed7 symbols1..10; deterministic full24-symbol table coverage; identical A sequences with analytic all-cell solution.
scientific_intent.accuracy_requirements: 14723 actual Int32 matrix values exact against source tiled CPU reference and independent Int64 rowwise DP. Reconstructed optimal alignment consumes both sequences and reproduces terminal score. Identical-A analytical formula checks every cell. All five raw artifacts pass both GPU references.
scientific_intent.input_size_regime: Full matrices65²,97²,33²; full16×16 tiles only, square sequences as native requires. Twenty complete repeated batches with input reset outside timing.
scientific_intent.precision_sensitivity: Exact bounded signed Int32 integer scores and gap arithmetic, independent Int64 accumulation checks. No floating-point error, affine-gap scoring or unbounded-overflow claim.
scientific_intent.community_use_case: Protein sequence similarity and comparative sequence analysis, supported by explicit BLOSUM62 scoring. Synthetic symbols exercise the algorithm; no actual biological sequence dataset or biological discovery is claimed.
scientific_intent.description: Complete global alignment, including all interior and boundary scores and independent optimal-path cost witnesses. This is a regular lattice path problem classified in the coarse graph/DP family; the implementation motif is explicitly dense tiled wavefront, not sparse irregular traversal.
scientific_intent.provenance: Unchanged native kernels and genuine existing CUDA.jl recurrence agree. Existing CUDA.jl uses one global kernel per cell anti-diagonal; KA/JACC follow native shared-memory tiles. Source gap scoring is linear, and initialized negative boundaries establish global rather than local alignment.
